apps.localizedDescription: Stremio — a modern media center for movies, series, live TV and web channels. Expand your content library with the add-on system. Requires iPhone and iPad, iOS 13.0+. NOTE: Some features such as Apple Login and Handoff do not work in the sideloaded version.

versions.localizedDescription:
Features

- Redesigned toast notifications with adaptive layouts and Liquid Glass styling on supported systems.
- Added dismissible toast cards with swipe gestures and stacked notifications.
- Added in-app notifications and modals with artwork and action buttons.

Fixes

- Dialogs now appear one at a time, preventing announcements, profile selection, subtitle prompts and add-on confirmations from conflicting.
- Preserved rounded-button styling on Mac, including Liquid Glass effects on supported versions and custom backgrounds on macOS 12.

New

- Added an option in Appearance settings to show titles below catalog posters.
- Play HTTP, HTTPS and magnet links directly by pasting them into Search.
- Added an experimental version streaming server which was rewritten in rust, available in Advanced settings and requiring an app restart.
- Added Native Player as an external player, with playback progress syncing back to Stremio.

Fixes

- Fixed title-preview action buttons when using the app as a guest.
- Torrent status now shows peer counts and download speed even when a stream has no file index.
- Clarified warnings explaining why software decoding is being used (interlaced videos).

New

- Playback speed is now remembered separately for each stream.
- Selected audio and subtitle tracks are remembered for each stream, including when subtitles are turned off.
- Subtitle delay is remembered for each stream, and Live Sync changes apply immediately.
- External subtitles can now be moved vertically with a position control.

Redesigned

- Add-on cards on iOS and macOS now have a cleaner layout with clearer actions.
- The add-on installation flow now opens as a content-sized sheet with an improved layout and clearer trust information.

Improvements

- Infuse playback progress now syncs back to Stremio.
- Player controls better respect safe areas, camera regions and different screen layouts.
- Subtitles no longer overlap playback buttons.
- Torrent status no longer conflicts with the title, while loading statistics remain correctly positioned.

Fixes

- Fixed the player hanging when opened on iOS 15.
- Fixed the play button remaining hidden after seeking.
- The F key now toggles fullscreen on Mac.
- Fixed ASS subtitles not rendering correctly in KSPlayer.
- Fixed player filter and dropdown buttons sometimes ignoring taps.
- Fixed title-preview actions being compressed and removed unnecessary spacing when filters are hidden.
- Fixed add-ons showing an incorrect protected warning after being uninstalled.
- Fixed loading torrent statistics appearing in the wrong position.
- Fixed profile PIN errors disappearing too quickly; the error now remains until the next input.
- Capitalized add-on types when a translation is unavailable.

New

- Calendar with month navigation and a daily agenda of upcoming episodes.
- Discover previews: tap a title to see its details inline, with trailer, library, watched and rating actions, without leaving Discover.
- Add-ons that receive your watch activity now show a warning and ask you to confirm before you install them.
- Support for foldable iPhones, with adaptive layouts for playback, login, account, profile picker and stream lists that keep content clear of the camera area.
- Hover, focus and press feedback on posters.

Redesigned

- Settings: grouped by task, with dedicated pages and adaptive sidebar navigation.
- Title details: richer metadata, new action buttons, artwork that fades into the background and a consistent info line for episodes.
- Player controls on iOS and macOS, with adaptive layouts, glass styling and refreshed Next Episode and Skip Intro popups.
- Subtitle menu: picking a language now selects its first subtitle automatically.
- Subtitle Live Sync (Supporters): cue search, applied delay and cue timing details.
- Profile picker (Supporters) on iOS.
- Native menus replace the custom dropdown sheets on iOS and macOS.
- Poster sizes and loading placeholders now match across all catalogs.
- Updated add-ons icon in the navigation bar and profile menu.

Improvements

- Discover shows every filter a catalog supports, sizes its filter bar to fit and shows an error when a page fails to load.
- Discover shows a loading indicator while more titles load and keeps your focus in place.
- Stream lists tell apart several configured copies of the same add-on.
- Library keeps its state when you switch tabs and shows a loading state until it's ready.
- Downloads: better retries and HTTP error handling. Resuming works correctly after a cancel, and storage cleanup only touches downloads.
- Settings stays in sync with the app: external player choices, Low Data Mode status and stream filter presets.
- Settings shows subtitle opacity as a percentage, rows show their current value, and only player options your device supports are listed.
- Your seek duration setting is now used everywhere, including hold-to-seek.
- Cinemeta configuration opens inside the app.
- Faster title details, stream lists, player and subtitle rendering.
- On iPad and Mac, selecting the current sidebar item again behaves like tapping the current tab.
- On iPad, action menus open from the button you tapped.
- Larger close buttons, toolbars that follow the app's tint, and chip rows that fade out at the edges.

Fixes

- Subtitles: fixed overlapping cues, automatic track selection (including embedded tracks), style changes not applying, format detection, handling of broken files and duplicate subtitle entries.
- More reliable video file matching for subtitles.
- Audio fallback now respects your secondary language preference.
- Catalog titles no longer repeat across pages.
- Fixed Discover filters, catalog links, navigation state and scroll position when you open a new catalog.
- Player: fixed it reporting ready too early, wrong loading transitions, timeline marker positions, native player presentation, the navigation bar showing during playback and back button spacing on iPhone. Also fixed the Next Episode popup on narrow screens and leftover screens after closing the player.
- External players no longer leave stale callbacks behind after playback.
- No more misleading error messages while offline, and better handling of library sync errors.
- Login: fixed placeholders, the password visibility toggle, keyboard focus, cancelling link login and the sign-in button position on Mac.
- Opening an episode directly keeps series navigation, and episode progress bars are correct.
- Spoiler episode thumbnails stay blurred.
- Fixed where catalog loading rows appear, the watched indicator overlapping badges and poster selection sticking after a tap on iPhone.
- Settings: fixed layout after rotation on iPad, dropdown sizing and rows collapsing with an avatar.
- Fixed tool

Dusklight brings a classic adventure natively to iPhone and iPad with modern rendering, flexible controls, quality-of-life options, and ongoing updates from the Twilit Realm team.

You must provide a dump of your own copy of the original game to play.

Dusklight 2.0 is here! This update brings mod support, an in-game mod browser, and our own built-in randomizer, alongside more polish, performance improvements, and ways to play. Thank you to everyone who helped make it happen!

Mods and built-in mods

- Added: Mod support! Install gameplay mods, asset replacements, and texture packs as .dusk bundles, and manage them from the Mods menu. (Modders: check out our modding documentation: https://github.com/TwilitRealm/dusklight/blob/main/docs/modding.md!)
- Added: An in-game mod browser: search for mods, view information and screenshots, and download and install without leaving Dusklight.
- Added: Mod update checks, release notes, and a quick way to update all mods.
- Added: Drag and drop .dusk mods onto the Dusklight window to install them.
- Added: Enable, disable, and reload mods in-game, with dependency handling and per-mod settings and logs.
- Added: Built-in Dusklight Randomizer, our own randomizer with seed generation, settings presets, shareable permalinks, and more.
  - Customize which items are shuffled, including shop items, NPC gifts, Golden Bugs, Poe Souls, Hidden Skills, and dungeon keys.
  - Randomize entrances to dungeons, boss rooms, caves, interiors, and overworld areas.
  - Choose starting equipment, skip the prologue and other sequences, and customize the requirements for reaching Hyrule Castle.
  - Detailed randomizer spoiler logs to help when you get stuck, with in-game export options for logs and seed data.
- Added: Built-in Cosmetics mod: customize Link's outfits, hair and equipment, Wolf Link, Epona, Midna, and HUD colors.

For mod creators

- Added: Asset-only mods: replace disc files, individual files inside .arc archives, and textures without writing code or repacking an entire game archive.
- Added: Powerful native C++ mods with direct access to game code and built-in mod services. Use hooks on game functions to add or change nearly anything.
- Added: Luau script mods for simpler UI, settings, and configurable asset replacements, without requiring native mod builds.
- Added: Versioned services and dependencies, allowing mods to be compatible across Dusklight versions and even provide features for other mods to build on.
- Added: A standalone mod SDK and project template, with easy builds for all supported platforms. (Quick start: https://github.com/TwilitRealm/dusklight/blob/main/docs/modding.md#quick-start-native-mods)
- Added: Custom game modes, with separate save files and control over starting and loading a game.
- Added: Custom actors, stage edits, player spawns, and item rewards for gameplay mods.
- Added: Custom dialogue and message flows, including new choices, events, full-color text, and gradients.
- Added: Custom mod windows, dialogs, controls, notifications, and interface themes.
- Added: Audio replacement APIs for sound effects, instrument samples, and streamed music. (audio API: https://github.com/TwilitRealm/dusklight/blob/main/sdk/include/mods/svc/audio_res.h, JAudio documentation: https://github.com/TwilitRealm/dusklight/blob/main/docs/jaudio.md)

- Added: Native file pickers, persistent storage, and networking services for mods.

versions.localizedDescription:
**BCD is in alpha:** an early stage of development, before beta. Many games run, many do not yet, and things can break between builds. When a game fails, please send a log.

> **Everything new in this release is experimental and has been tried on only a few devices so far.** It may work great on yours, or it may not work at all. Either way, a log helps a lot.

> **Tried a game on an earlier build? Reset its settings first.** On the game's page: **Options › Recommended settings › Reset to Recommended**. The recommended list changed for 17 games in this release.

This build brings everything since 0.1.712:
- a fix for the launch crash on the iOS 27.2 beta;
- Steam Cloud saves that games could not see;
- a round of fixes from the logs you sent and from the #game-reports channel;
- LiveContainer 3.8.14 support for the built-in JIT helper;
- live logs over Wi-Fi;
- an option to see the game's cursor in Mouse-look;
- a fix for bcd.cfg losing every setting over one odd character, fixes for videos in 32-bit games and two new switches that save CPU time.

## Fixed: the launch crash on the iOS 27.2 beta

0.1.712 crashed at once on the iOS 27.2 beta when a Steam account was signed in. Two of Apple's date comparisons are new in iOS 27.2, and the beta says it is 27.2 without having them yet. BCD now compares dates in a way that gives the same result on every iOS. The build now also fails on my build Mac if a new call of that kind ever comes in.

## Steam Cloud: saves the game could not see (changed default)

Some games keep their saves through Steam Cloud's own interface: The Binding of Isaac, Don't Starve and Slay the Spire 2, for example. Players reported "no cloud saves" in such games. BCD downloaded the files, but the game started a new profile.

- **Why:** in a BCD Dock session such a game sees only the files Valve's client lists in its own file list (`remotecache.vdf`). BCD downloaded your saves next to that list but did not add them to it. The game saw no saves, started a new profile, and that new profile could later be uploaded over the old one.
- **What changed:** after each comparison, before the game starts, BCD now writes Valve's list when a save that is the same on the device and in the cloud is missing from it. A game whose list already names its saves, and a game with no such saves, gets no write. The rewrite existed before, but it was off.
- **Going back:** in **Settings › All settings**, `env.MADEIRA_STEAM_CLOUD_REMOTECACHE` (Steam Cloud: Valve's client's file list) offers three choices:
  - **When a save is missing from it** (the new default);
  - **After every comparison**;
  - **Never** (as before).
- **Not covered:** games that keep their saves in their own folders through Steam's automatic cloud (Cult of the Lamb, for example). If yours lost its save, please send the log of a start right after you see the empty save.
- The log now counts, at each comparison, how many saves the list names and how many it misses. It counts only and names no files.

## Fixed in games (from the logs you sent and #game-reports)

Each was made from a log and checked by tests on a Mac.

- **Cyberpunk 2077** now gets far: on one 12 GB iPhone it played for one to two minutes at about 30 FPS. Then Metal ended it for a blend setting it does not allow on a second render target. BCD now builds such a pipeline without that blend.
- **The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+** still crashed with the 32-bit memory settings that 0.1.712 put in its recommended settings: the game's memory library asks for memory without naming an upper limit, and the settings only looked at requests that name one. Such a request now also stays inside the game's own part of the address space.
- **Hitman: Blood Money** stopped in its start-up code every time (14 logs). Its recommended settings now make BCD's translator check every instruction against the program's current bytes (`env.FEX_SMCCHECKS = full`). It is slower.
- **Resident Evil 7, The Witcher 3, Just Cause 3, Devil May Cry 5 and other Direct3D 11 games that hang the GPU:** the 64-bit Direct3D 11 layer BCD ships was built before a fix in its own source for draws with tessellation or geometry shaders. With that fix missing, a batch of such draws could keep the GPU busy until iOS reset it.
  - BCD carries a newer build of that layer, the "fresh" set. `env.MADEIRA_DXMT_FRESH = 1` in a game's settings uses it.
  - Resident Evil 7's recommended settings now carry the line: a player's freeze at one place was gone with it.
  - For other games, auto-tune offers it once after a start that ended with the GPU hang, except for the heavy games that have settings of their own, such as GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2.
- **ULTRAKILL and other games played with a mouse or trackpad:** pressing Escape ended the mouse lock, and the mouse then stayed dead until you switched apps. When iPadOS ends a lock BCD still wants, BCD now takes it as your own release of the pointer. `env.MADEIRA_POINTER_LOCK_END = 0` turns this off.
- **FINAL FANTASY TACTICS - The Ivalice Chronicles and Kingdom Come: Deliverance II** stopped on a Direct3D 12 pipeline library. Their recommended settings now turn BCD's pipeline library on (`d3d12-pipeline-library = 1`).
- **Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter (demo):** the demo has its own Steam App ID, so the full game's recommended settings never reached it. They do now.
- **FINAL FANTASY XIII** showed its "not enough video memory" box. It reads the 128 MB that Windows' DirectX diagnostics reports, and its recommended settings now report 2000 MB.
- **S.T.A.L.K.E.R. (Shadow of Chernobyl, Clear Sky, Call of Pripyat) through BCD Dock:** the first Play ran only the game's DirectX setup, which failed, and you had to restart BCD. BCD already ships what that setup installs, so the setup is now skipped and the first Play starts the game.
- **Stardew Valley** stopped after one frame while GOG Galaxy's online library waited for a Galaxy program that is not there. Its recommended settings switch that library off for this game. GOG's online features are not available then.
- **MudRunner (Epic)** started without BCD's sign-in helper, so its Epic online services had no sign-in and the game faulted. It now starts through the helper.
- **Borderlands 2** copied a whole vertex buffer for every draw (13 to 21 FPS in a player's report). It now gets the Direct3D 9 change that copies only what a draw reads (`env.DXMT_D9_VB_RANGE = 1`, see 0.1.712).
- **Little Nightmares Enhanced Edition** on devices whose GPU cannot read compressed textures (A14 and older): coloured noise on every texture. BCD now decodes those textures on the CPU for it. Devices with less than 10 GB of RAM also get the memory settings of the one run that lasted.
- **Kingdom Come: Deliverance** (the first game) was closed by iOS at the memory limit on an 8 GB phone. Devices with less than 10 GB of RAM now get the swap file of the other 8 GB rows.
- **Dead Space 2:** EA's activation program read garbled text and the game ended. Its recommended settings try the emulator's exact x87 mode. This is an experiment.
- **Crysis (2007):** the 64-bit program stops in `CrySystem.dll` on a pointer it keeps in 32 bits. Use the 32-bit program, `Bin32\Crysis.exe`. The game's page says so.
- **Games with a large program at a fixed address** (DRAGON BALL FighterZ, eFootball PES 2021):
  - **The cause:** in some starts of BCD, iOS puts memory of its own where the program must load, and the game does not start.
  - **What changed:** BCD now also uses the free room below it when that room holds the program's own size.
  - **When it still happens:** quit BCD completely (swipe it away in the app switcher), open it again and start the game. iOS lays memory out anew at every start.
- **Steam games whose files Steam prepares for your account (copy protection), through BCD Dock:**
  - **The stop:** in some starts of BCD, Valve's helper service ends at once after its first call to Windows' service manager is lost, and the start fails with code 49 (Mafia II, Call of Duty: Black Ops and others).
  - **The experiment:** when that happens in a service manager BCD Dock started itself, it now starts one fresh service manager and tries the service once more. This costs about 25 seconds, and only on a start that would fail anyway. `env.MADEIRA_DOCK_CEG_SCM_RESTART = 0` turns it off.
  - **The text:** the code 55 message now says that this does not happen in every start of BCD.
- **Path of Exile 2** could open neither its shader cache nor its pipeline cache:
  - **The stop:** the game opens each cache as a 100 GB view over a small file and grows it as it writes. Windows allows that. BCD refused it (`c000001f` in the log).
  - **What changed:** BCD now extends the file to the end of such a view, at most 16 GB by default (`env.MADEIRA_SECTION_VIEW_CAP_GB`). The empty part takes no storage. Only a request BCD refused before takes this path; every other one is handled as before.
  - **Going back:** `env.MADEIRA_SECTION_VIEW_GROW = 0` brings the refusal back.
- **Logs:** Grim Dawn's and Neon Abyss's recommended settings now put the game's own log into the next Send Log, so their stops can be found. They fix nothing yet.

## LiveContainer 3.8.14: the built-in JIT helper works again (from a pull request)

LiveContainer 3.8.14 changed how it hands a guest app its helper. 0.1.712 did not recognise the new way, so inside LiveContainer the built-in JIT helper and the helper memory stayed off ("not-ready: noHook" in the log). BCD now sees the prepared helper. LiveContainer's Helper Process Support, a full-screen launch and the install-time preparation are still required. (pull request #74)

## Live logs over Wi-Fi (from a pull request, off by default)

**Settings › Logs › Live logs** shows the log of the running session on a computer on the same Wi-Fi, as it is written, for example in a browser. (pull request #71)

- Only devices on the same Wi-Fi network can connect, and at most four at a time.
- The address carries a secret key. **Copy live log URL** copies the address with the key in it. The key changes each time you turn live logs on and each time BCD starts. Without the key the log is refused.
- The log holds your account names and folder paths. Turn this on only on a Wi-Fi you trust. On a café's or a hotel's Wi-Fi, other people on that network could try to connect, and the key is what keeps them out.

## Mouse-look: see the game's own cursor in its menus (new, off unless set)

With Mouse-look as the finger mode your finger turns the camera, and BCD drew no cursor, so a game's menus had no visible pointer. In **Settings › All settings**, `env.MADEIRA_RELATIVE_CURSOR` (Mouse-look: show the game's cursor in its menus) changes that:
- the game's own cursor is shown while the game shows it, in its menus;
- it is hidden while the game hides it, in play.

Some things stay the same:
- A tap still does not click in Mouse-look. Use the on-screen buttons, or switch to Trackpad to press a menu item.
- It works for games started directly, not in a Windows desktop or BCD Dock session.
- Restart BCD after you change it.

## Other fixes and new switches

- **Settings no longer lose bcd.cfg over one character:**
  - **The fault:** one character in bcd.cfg that is not UTF-8 (a comment saved by an editor on a PC, for example) made Settings show no keys. The next change in Settings then rewrote the file with only that one key, and every other setting was gone.
  - **What changed:** Settings now reads such a file and writes every other line back as it was. A file that exists but cannot be read is left alone, not rewritten.
- **Videos in 32-bit games** (and in 64-bit games only with `env.MADEIRA_WIN64_FRESH = 1`): three fixes in Windows' media libraries.
  - A video whose frames the GPU has no format for no longer loses its video output, which left the video without a single frame. Its frames now come through ordinary memory.
  - The Windows Media reader no longer crashes after it was refused a compressed stream (the movie player of KiriKiri games, for example).
  - Copying a frame into a Direct3D 9 surface no longer waits for the GPU to read that surface back first.
- **Direct3D 11 games that keep a CPU core busy asking the GPU "done yet?"** (new, off unless set):
  - **The problem:** some games ask whether the GPU has finished in a tight loop, 100,000 to 15 million times a second. BCD's logs show it in 21 games, such as Schedule I, Palworld and Rocket League.
  - **The switch:** with `env.MADEIRA_D3D11_QUERY_PARK = 1` such a burst waits for the GPU's signal, at most 1 ms each time, instead of spinning. A single question never waits.
  - **Where it works:** 32-bit games, and 64-bit games with `env.MADEIRA_D3D11_SRC = 1` or `env.MADEIRA_DXMT_FRESH = 1`. The default 64-bit Direct3D 11 layer does not have it.
- **Less work for the x86 translator when a game unmaps streamed data** (new, off unless set):
  - **The problem:** when a game unmaps a file view that never held code, the translator still locked and searched its translated code for that range. Some games do this tens of thousands of times in a session (Red Dead Redemption 2, GTA IV and V, Fallout 4).
  - **The switch:** `env.MADEIRA_FEX_SECTION_SKIP = 1` skips that search for such a view.

## Auto-tune

11 rules are new and 7 changed. Each has a log it was made from.

- **New fixes it can try:**
  - a Direct3D 11 game whose GPU hung while it drew gets the fresh Direct3D 11 set (not the heavy games, see above);
  - Hitman: Blood Money's start-up stop gets the instruction check;
  - an Epic game that ended in a fault in Epic's online services, and had not started through BCD's sign-in helper, gets the helper;
  - a 32-bit program whose oversized data section took the code memory's execute right behind it gets that protection kept inside the module.
- **Answers that say what to do:**
  - a stop on GOG Galaxy's online library: the line that switches it off;
  - the copy-protection service stop (code 49 after the lost call, and code 55 after about 100 seconds): what is known and that it does not happen in every start;
  - a game that waits for an NVIDIA card's answer that never comes: send the log;
  - a device whose address space is too small for the emulator itself: the increased memory limit (GetMoreRam with SideStore or LiveContainer, or a paid developer account), or that the device is too small;
  - Cyberpunk 2077's blend stop and Isaac's memory outside its part: update BCD.
- **Narrowed:**
  - Unity games are no longer offered BCD's OpenGL;
  - a game that ran out of memory is no longer told its Steam files are missing;
  - the emulator's own address-space stop is no longer counted as a runtime fault;
  - the fixed-address program stop now gives the advice above instead of "Update BCD".

## Recommended settings

The list went from 96 to 98: 6 games are new and 11 changed.

- **New:**
  - Dead Space 2
  - Crysis
  - Kingdom Come: Deliverance
  - Grim Dawn
  - Little Nightmares Enhanced Edition
  - Neon Abyss
- **Updated:**
  - Resident Evil 7 biohazard
  - Trails in the Sky 1st Chapter
  - FINAL FANTASY TACTICS - The Ivalice Chronicles
  - MudRunner
  - Stardew Valley
  - Hitman: Blood Money
  - S.T.A.L.K.E.R. (X-Ray engine games)
  - The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth (notes only)
  - Borderlands 2
  - Kingdom Come: Deliverance II
  - FINAL FANTASY XIII

## The November 2026 Steam client in BCD Dock, and why you don't need Steam for Windows to play (experimental)

Nothing in this part changed since 0.1.712. It is here again for everyone who skipped that release.

### What BCD Dock is
- BCD Dock starts your Steam games through **Valve's own Steam client library** (`steamclient64.dll`, the file the full Steam app for Windows also uses). It runs inside BCD without Steam's window, its web browser (Chromium) and its library.
- BCD Dock signs in with your own Steam sign-in. Valve's client then does what a game needs from Steam, as it does on a PC:
  - the online sign-in and the check that you own the game;
  - the game's Steam calls and any Steam DRM the game carries;
  - the per-account programs some games need (BCD Dock asks the client to prepare them before the start);
  - signing in offline;
  - Friends in games, when you turn them on in **Settings › Accounts › Steam**.
- BCD Dock is not a Steam emulator and bypasses nothing. Without Valve's sign-in and licence answer, a game does not start.

### What the November 2026 client adds
- **Settings › BCD Dock › Steam client** offers three builds of Valve's client:
  - **Jan 2026**, the default;
  - **Sep 2026**: for games that ask for a newer Steam interface than January's has, such as Grim Dawn, Hades II and Enshrouded. No Friends;
  - **Nov 2026**: the client Valve published on 13 November 2026.
- **Newer Steam interfaces.** Nov 2026 has five interfaces that the January client lacks: `SteamUser024`, `SteamInput007`, `SteamNetworkingSockets013`, `SteamGameServer016` and `SteamMatchMakingServers003`. A game built with a newer Steam library can stop at its start with "Missing interface adapter", with "No SteamUtils011" or with a "Steam is not running" box. Nov 2026 has the newer interfaces such a game asks for. A game may still ask for something newer than Valve's client of 13 November has.
- **Friends** work with Nov 2026, as with Jan 2026. Sep 2026 has none.
- **BCD's suggestions** name Nov 2026 when a game stops because its Steam library is newer than the client (for `SteamUtils011`, Sep 2026 has the interface too).
- **Switching** moves your installed games, saves and settings to the chosen client, and you can switch back at any time. The old client's folder is renamed and kept. Nothing is deleted.
- **A build BCD Dock does not know is refused before sign-in** with report code 30, not guessed at. BCD Dock checks the exact client file and the exact calls it makes into it, build by build. Valve moved four of the client's internal calls (the two ownership questions and the two offline sign-in calls) by one slot in this build, so each build has its own table.
- **Tried so far, on one iPhone:**
  - the switch to Nov 2026 and back;
  - games started through BCD Dock;
  - a game whose per-account program Steam prepares;
  - an offline start;
  - Friends;
  - a game that stopped on a missing Steam interface.
- **January 2026 stays the default.** Nov 2026 is less tested. Choose it when a game needs it. If a game no longer starts with it, switch back.

### Why you don't need Steam for Windows to play
- **The game already talks to Valve's real client.** Sign-in, ownership, Steam's calls, per-account programs, offline play and Friends all go through the same client library that BCD Dock runs. The full Steam app adds a window around that library. A game does not need the window.
- **Memory.** Steam's window is a web browser. On the one iPhone tried, it held:
  - 2.3 to 3.4 GB of the 8 GB iOS gives BCD;
  - much of BCD's address space;
  - a JIT pool of up to 1.1 GB for its own code.

  Heavy games need all of that for themselves. Through BCD Dock they get it.
- **Each game's own BCD settings.** Through BCD Dock every game starts with its recommended settings and the ones you set on its page. A game started from Steam for Windows runs inside Steam's session, with that session's settings. X-Plane 12, started that way, found no Vulkan driver and quit after nine seconds.
- **BCD's own library covers the rest:** downloads and updates, DLC you own, beta versions, Workshop items, Steam Cloud saves and Launch options.

### When Steam for Windows can still help
These are things BCD itself does not do:
- buying games or DLC in the Steam store;
- Steam's own settings and account pages, and Steam's community pages;
- your friends list and chat outside a game (BCD offers Friends in a game);
- your achievements: BCD does not show them;
- updating a game that Valve's client installed in its own library folder. BCD lists and starts such a game but does not update it.

Steam's app on your phone, or Steam's website, can do most of these too. Steam for Windows (experimental, off unless you turn it on in **Settings › BCD Dock › Steam for Windows**) is for those things, not for playing games.

## Known issues

- **Cyberpunk 2077:** past the blend stop, the next limit is likely memory. In the logs it reached 7.4 to 7.8 GB of the 8 GB limit within two minutes.
- **Steam Cloud for games with automatic cloud saves in their own folders** (Cult of the Lamb, for example): not solved. A log helps.
- **Copy-protected Steam games through BCD Dock** can still fail with code 49 or 55 in some starts of BCD. Quitting BCD completely and starting again helps in many cases.

Install help, game reports and ideas: the BCD-Games Discord is open, https://discord.gg/43TmupTVug

## Graphics and memory

**Faster frame submission.** MoltenVK now turns each frame into Metal work on its own thread instead of on the graphics thread, so the graphics thread spends almost no time submitting a frame. Framebuffers are now freed only after the GPU has finished with them, which this needed. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Freed textures give their memory back.** Large texture allocations now get memory of their own, which goes back to iOS when the texture is freed. Before, one texture still in use kept a whole 64 MB block, and One Piece held 2.3 GB of blocks for 643 MB of textures. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Upload buffer space comes back sooner.** The texture upload buffer gives back finished space after every full GPU wait, where it held it until the next frame and swapped in a new buffer instead.

**No stall on the first new shader.** The shader compiler's one-time setup now happens at boot. It used to land in gameplay, on the first shader a game hadn't shown before. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Black Ops II weapon.** The weapon in your hands no longer draws with its triangles over each other.

**Resolution scale below 100%.** Some copies between images ran a pixel past the edge and stopped the game with "Verification failed". They are now trimmed to fit.

**Half-precision shader math from RPCS3.** Shaders now handle 16-bit floating point the way the PS3's GPU does, with RPCS3's newest fixes.

## Faster

**Short waits are the right length.** The timer scale was never set on iOS, so on phones whose counter runs at 1 GHz every short wait lasted about a 33rd of what was meant. It is now set before the emulator starts. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Less heat while SPU code compiles.** With Pause Game During SPU Compilation, every paused thread spun at full speed for the whole compile. Paused threads now sleep.

**Loops move to compiled code sooner.** New SPU code runs in the interpreter while it compiles in the background. A loop that started just before its code was ready now switches to the compiled code as soon as it is done, where it stayed in the interpreter, ten to fifty times slower, until it ended.

**SPU loops stay compiled.** Loops that branch back to their own program's start, which The Last of Us uses a lot, no longer go through the dispatcher on every pass.

**No lock on every SPU memory transfer.** A leftover debug log took a global lock on every SPU memory transfer in games that use SPURS. It cost The Last of Us 3.3% of all SPU time.

**Game updates keep compiled SPU code.** Installing a game update no longer compiles every SPU program again.

## Games

**The Last of Us.**
- Its four busiest SPU programs now have hand-written ARM versions that give the same results. The heaviest, a shading filter, runs more than twice as fast.
- RPCS3's recommended patches are on by default. They fix a crash and a softlock, help performance and let resolution scaling work.
- A freeze where the game waits on a job list that nothing restarts is now detected and the list restarted.
- The SPU compile pause stays on for every version of the game, since turning it off froze cold boots on the Mac.

**Uncharted 3.** It uses the same job manager as The Last of Us and froze the same way. The same restart now covers it.

**Killzone 3.** It now uses SPU Inline Interrupt Idioms, as on Android. It also gets Android 1.7's other per-game settings, and so does Ratchet & Clank: Tools of Destruction.

**God of War III.** SPU writes that store back unchanged data no longer cost the other SPUs their reservations. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

## Library and storage

**A games folder you can copy into.** Copy a game folder into Files › ARMSX3 › games and it shows in the library the next time you open ARMSX3, or straight away when you pull down to refresh.
